title: Gradients and Directional Derivatives
text:
For a differentiable function (f:^2),
\[
\nabla f(x,y)
=
\left\langle f_x(x,y),f_y(x,y)\right\rangle.
\]
The gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent.






Geometric intuition





The gradient is perpendicular to the level curve through the point. It points toward increasing values of the function.

title: Gradients and Directional Derivatives
text:
Example
Let
\[ f(x,y)=x^2+2y^2. \]






Hint





Calculate the two partial derivatives separately.









Solution





We obtain
\[
f_x=2x,\qquad f_y=4y,
\]
so
\[
\nabla f(x,y)=\langle 2x,4y\rangle.
\]
At \((1,2)\), this becomes
\[
\nabla f(1,2)=\langle 2,8\rangle.
\]

title: Teaching
text:
I view teaching and learning as fundamentally human endeavors. My goal is to create a classroom in which students feel comfortable exploring unfamiliar ideas while developing the precision and rigor needed to do mathematics independently.
I aim to connect abstract mathematical concepts to geometric intuition, concrete examples, and visual representations whenever possible.
For a full essay on my instructional approach, here is my teaching philosophy statement.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching experience
My teaching experience includes calculus, multivariable calculus, and differential equations, both as a teaching assistant and as an instructor of record.
As an instructor, I have designed course materials, assignments, and computational demonstrations to help students connect mathematical theory with applications.

title: Research
text:
Current Research
My doctoral work concerns estimates for the bottom of the spectrum of the Laplacian under integral Ricci curvature bounds. This work explores how curvature information, even when controlled in an integral sense, can constrain spectral properties.

title: Cole Durham
text:
I am currently a Ph.D. candidate in mathematics at the University of Connecticut, advised by Ovidiu Munteanu, with an expected graduation date of May 2027.
My research explores relationships between geometric and analytic properties of Riemannian manifolds. In particular, I have done work relating to the spectrum of the Laplacian under bounded integral Ricci curvature.
I have had the great fortune to teach roughly 1000 students throughout my 11 semesters at UConn across Calculus I-III, Calculus for Business and Economics, and Elementary Differential Equations. Being an educator will always be passionate about.
